title: BlackRock CEO Says Data Center Freeze Could Push U.S. Into Recession
key_facts: BlackRock chief executive Larry Fink spoke to CNBC on Wednesday after BlackRock's third-quarter results.
He said a moratorium on data centres would put the US in recession.
He said most criticism is 'misinformation' and data centres are creating more jobs than ever.
Opposition to data centres is rising before the 3 November midterms over power bills, water and financing visibility.
The PJM grid, serving about 67 million people, expects demand from large computing sites to reach 29 gigawatts by 2030.
Analysts estimate annual AI capital spending could exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
quote_evidence: "If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession," he said.
"Data centers are not the problem. They're creating more new jobs than ever before," he said.
why_it_matters_hint: A major investor links the AI buildout to the health of the whole US economy as data centres turn political.
notes: CNBC original not read; BigGo Finance relays the interview. BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners recently completed a roughly $40 billion Aligned Data Centers deal (BigGo), which is the conflict-of-interest context.
